chapters.summary: Council Staff welcomes attendees to the Committee on Immigration hearing. They remind everyone to silence electronic devices and adhere to protocol before the Chair begins the proceedings.
chapters.title: Council Staff opens the Committee on Immigration hearing

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to today's New York City Council vote from the Committee on Immigration.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, I'd like to remind everyone to please silence their electronic devices and at no point is anyone to approach the dais.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, we are ready to begin.

chapters.summary: Chair Elsie Encarnación introduces the resolution, Councilmember Farrah Lewis's Resolution 626. The resolution calls on the U.S. Senate and the President to pass S-4814, requiring the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for Temporary Protected Status (TPS).
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación introduces Resolution 626 regarding Haiti TPS

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Elsie Encarnacion, Deputy Whip of the New York City Council and Chair of the Committee on Immigration.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Today, we are voting on Councilmember Farrah Lewis's Resolution 626, which calls upon the United States Senate to pass and the President to sign S-4814 to require the

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for Temporary Protected Status, or TPS.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The committee heard this resolution on September 22nd and received ample testimony in support of this bill.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: We are joined today by my council colleagues, Councilmember Aviles, Councilmember Hanks, Councilmember Joseph, and Council...

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Oh, and that's it, right?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I was going to keep going.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And some to be determined at a later time.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación explains that TPS is a designation granted by the Secretary of Homeland Security to countries facing extraordinary temporary conditions, such as armed conflict or environmental disasters. She notes that TPS protects immigrants from detention and deportation based on their immigration status.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación defines Temporary Protected Status (TPS)

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: TPS is a designation made by the Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security for countries experiencing ongoing armed conflict, environmental disasters, or other extraordinary and temporary conditions.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Immigrants have been granted TPS.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: that have been granted TPS are protected against detention and deportation on the basis of their immigration status.

chapters.summary: The Chair details the severe crises Haiti has faced since 2010, including earthquakes, epidemics, and political instability. She highlights the critical issue that the Trump administration terminated Haiti's TPS status in July 2026.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación details Haiti's history and the termination of TPS

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: In 2010, Haiti first received a TPS designation after experiencing a massive and devastating earthquake, and since then has suffered through

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: an epidemic, another earthquake, a tropical storm, a presidential assassination, the resignation of their prime minister, and widespread gang violence.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Despite these atrocities, the Trump administration terminated Haiti's TPS status in July 2026.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: In a cruel twist of irony, the U.S.

chapters.summary: Encarnación points out the irony of the U.S. Department of State issuing travel advisories warning against Haiti due to crime and kidnapping. She notes that despite these warnings, the administration has been deporting Haitians into a country facing severe violence.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación contrasts U.S. travel warnings with recent deportations

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Department of State's latest travel advisory about Haiti warns U.S.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Citizens against traveling there for any reasons due to the risk associated with crime, terrorism, kidnapping, unrest, and limited health care.

chapters.summary: The Chair asserts that Haitian communities have significantly enriched New York City and that TPS recipients belong in New York, not in dangerous conditions abroad. She expresses pride in co-sponsoring the resolution.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación advocates for Haitian community inclusion in New York

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Yet, the administration has already deported more than 450 Haitians in recent weeks, landing them amid a surge in kidnapping and gang violence across Haiti.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Our Haitian communities have immeasurably enriched our city, and Haitian TPS recipients belong here in New York, not in harm's way.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación thanks the committee staff, including Nicole Cata and Rebecca Barilla, and acknowledges the work of her staff and colleagues who supported the hearing.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación thanks committee staff and colleagues

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I am proud to co-sponsor this resolution and thank Councilmember Lewis for introducing it.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I would like to thank the committee staff for their work on this hearing, including Senior Legislative Counsel Nicole Cata, Senior Legislative Policy Analyst Rebecca Barilla, Principal Financial

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Analyst Navi Baines and Assistant Finance Director Florentine Kabor.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Finally, I'd like to thank my staff, especially my chief of staff, Stephanie Herrera, and anyone working on the background to make this hearing run smoothly.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación concludes her introductory remarks and formally opens the floor to members who wish to make a statement regarding the resolution.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación opens the floor for statements

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I would like to open it to any members who would like to make a statement.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Rita C. Joseph begins her statement, thanking the Chair and Councilmember Farrah Lewis for carrying the resolution. She introduces the bill, which calls on the U.S. Senate to designate Haiti for temporary protective status through April 2029.
chapters.title: Councilmember Joseph speaks in support of the resolution

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Councilmember Joseph.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair, and thank you to my colleague, Councilmember Farrah Lewis, for carrying this resolution.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Today, we vote on a resolution calling on the United States Senate to pass and the President to sign S-4814.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: The bill does one simple thing.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: It requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protective status through April 2029.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: The families this bill protects live here.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Joseph emphasizes that the families protected by this bill live in New York. She notes that approximately 40,000 Haitian TPS holders reside in New York State, contributing as nurses, home health aides, and small business owners.
chapters.title: Councilmember Joseph details the impact of TPS on New York residents

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: About 40,000 Haitian TPS holders call New York State home, most of them in Brooklyn and Queens and in neighborhoods like the ones I represent.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They are nurses, home health aides.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They are parents of children in our public schools.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They pay taxes, run small businesses, and keep our hospital staff.

chapters.summary: Joseph explains that after the Supreme Court allowed the administration to end TPS for Haiti, job authorizations disappeared, leading to weekly deportation flights. She stresses that these flights send people to a country in crisis, marked by gang violence and institutional collapse.
chapters.title: Councilmember Joseph addresses the consequences of TPS termination

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: This summer, after the Supreme Court allowed the administration to end TPS for Haiti, those protections disappeared.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Our city has had to let go of employees who lost their job authorization.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And since August, deportation flights have left for Haiti every single week.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Those flights are going to a country in crisis, gang violence, kidnappings, and the collapse of basic institution.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: One recent attack killed 47 people, took a dozen hostages, including children.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Our own State Department warned Americans not to travel to Haiti.

chapters.summary: She argues that the U.S. cannot tell citizens it is too dangerous to visit Haiti while allowing neighbors to live there without protection. She notes that the decision rests with Congress, as judges cannot override the administration's decision.
chapters.title: Councilmember Joseph argues for consistency between U.S. warnings and immigration policy

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: We cannot tell our citizens it is too dangerous to visit and then tell our neighbors it's safe enough to live.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: The court said judges cannot override this decision.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That puts it squarely in Congress's hand.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Joseph states that the House has already acted on a companion bill and urges the Senate to act immediately. She concludes by stating that Haitians are New Yorkers and votes 'aye' on the resolution.
chapters.title: Councilmember Joseph concludes her testimony urging Senate action

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: The House has already acted.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: A bipartisan majority passed the companion bill in April.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: The president has said he wants to work with Congress and immigration.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Here's the place to start.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: The Senate must act, and it must act now.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Haitians are not temporary.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They are New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I proudly vote aye and urge my colleagues to do the same.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Merci, Ampil, and thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación thanks Councilmember Joseph and acknowledges the presence of Councilmember Brewer. She asks if there are any further requests for statements, concluding the testimony phase.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación acknowledges other members and closes statements

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Council Member.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I also like to acknowledge that we've been joined by Council Member Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Any last requests for statements?

chapters.summary: The Chair moves the meeting to take a roll call vote on the resolution. The Committee Clerk, Ben Jacobs, is called to the podium to conduct the vote.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación moves to roll call vote

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I now turn it over to...

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: I voted too early.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: You wrote it already.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: To take roll call.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Ben Jacobs, Committee Clerk, the City Council Committee on Immigration.

chapters.summary: The Committee Clerk initiates the roll call vote on Resolution 626, starting with Chair Encarnación.
chapters.title: Roll call vote on Resolution 626 begins

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: This is the roll call vote on Resolution 626.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación votes 'aye' on the resolution.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación votes 'aye'

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair Encarnacion.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Alexa Avilés votes 'aye', stating her support is in full and unapologetic solidarity with the Haitian community.
chapters.title: Councilmember Avilés votes 'aye'

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Aviles.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Proudly vote aye in standing in full and unapologetic solidarity with the Haitian community.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Gale A. Brewer votes 'aye', expressing strong support for the Haitian community.
chapters.title: Councilmember Brewer votes 'aye'

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Very supportive of the Haitian community.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Hanks.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Kamillah Hanks votes 'aye' on the resolution.
chapters.title: Councilmember Hanks votes 'aye'

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: I vote aye.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Rita C. Joseph votes 'aye' again.
chapters.title: Councilmember Joseph votes 'aye'

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Councilmember Joseph.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I vote aye again.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: The Committee Clerk announces that the resolution has been adopted with a vote of five in the affirmative and zero in the negative. Chair Encarnación thanks the members and closes the committee meeting.
chapters.title: Resolution 626 is adopted with a vote of five-zero

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: With a vote of five in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions, the item is adopted.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I now close this committee meeting.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Vote.

title: Committee on Immigration
topic: Require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for Temporary Protected Status ( S.4814)
